headline: UK cyber agency sees a rise in AI-run attacks that exploit old, simple weaknesses
summary: The National Cyber Security Centre says AI tools let attackers move faster and at low cost, using weaknesses such as default and weak passwords. Small businesses can close the same gaps.
body: The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) says it has seen a marked rise in AI-assisted cyber attacks since September 2026. In a blog post published on 24 November, it describes attackers using tools first built for authorised security testing. An AI plans each step, runs hacking tools against a target, checks the results and tries again. Some organisations lost services for a time, and some had systems broken into.

None of the weaknesses are new, the NCSC says. The change is speed: these tools attack quickly and persistently, at low cost. They can use default passwords, guess weak ones over and over, and go after systems left open to the internet.

The post speaks to security teams, yet the basics apply to any small business with a website, an online shop or staff logins. The NCSC tells organisations to find everything they have online, including old websites and equipment they’ve forgotten about. It also points to Cyber Essentials, which it says sets out the minimum technical controls the government recommends for organisations.
do_this: Change any default passwords on your website, online shop and business software, and replace weak ones.
List everything your business has online, including old websites, and ask if each one still needs to be public.
Keep your website and anything else people can reach over the internet updated, or ask your IT provider to.
